utterances.text: And then there 's a question of you: "Have you seen something? This is something, for instance, the brigades in the Skopje Defence command, including the 1st Guardist Brigade." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then Mr. Kuehnel says, for the record, that Mr. Despodov is shown a particular document. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree there that you didn't ask Mr. Kuehnel for his permission to ask questions? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that actually, in this specific case. I may very well have asked him because what you see in the brackets here as indiscernible might actually be my question to Mr. Kuehnel, and I would also like to draw your attention, Mr. Mettraux, to the fact that this record is not official record.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that specification, Mr. Bezruchenko, but do you agree that the thing you were asking Mr. Despodov whether he had seen or not, as is clear from the clarification given by Mr. Kuehnel, is in fact a document from the 11th of June of 2001? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the process of the interview, Mr. Despodov was shown a number of documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go down that page, you will see that you carry on with your questioning. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, in the specification of the very first question asked.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters kindly ask you, once again, to pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you can see, again, that there is it no involvement here of Mr. Kuehnel in your questioning of Mr. Despodov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, apparently not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as you can see, Mr. Bezruchenko, or would you agree that you just went on asking your questions to Mr. Despodov without asking for any permission or agreement on the part of Mr. Kuehnel? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that, Mr. Mettraux, because I simply don't remember. In fact, this agreement could have been reached with Mr. Kuehnel at the very beginning of the interview, and it does not necessarily mean that I would have to ask permission for each and every question, each and every time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see. If we go down the page, you will see there Mr. Kuehnel appears in the middle of the page, and he notes for the record that the witness, Mr. Despodov, is shown a copy of a map. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you just carry on with your question of Mr. Despodov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that the questioning of you of Mr. Despodov just goes on, and that Mr. Kuehnel intervenes, only at one point, not to allow a question, but simply to indicate that a particular marking should be made on the map can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The reason for that being the fact that this map was a military map with military symbols and specifications which required special attention and knowledge of certain details.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that as far as questioning is concerned, you just go on asking your question of Mr. Despodov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, in specification of the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that your questioning of Mr. Despodov just goes on uninterrupted by Mr. Kuehnel? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I was looking for at this point, apparently, was the description of positions of the battalion, and, of course, such a question would really be broken down in a big number of smaller questions to clarify certain points.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the only involvement of Mr. Kuehnel is to record for the transcript the fact that the witness was shown a map and that he made a marking on it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are discussing, if you are discussing such a complex document as a map, or, for that matter, some other military document, you would not normally limit your questions to one, because this is simply something which requires a lot of time, lot of attention, and a lot of details.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if I understand your answer properly, you would ask as many questions as you sought relevant for your own purposes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would ask as many questions as would be deemed appropriate by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that at no point during this questioning did Mr. Kuehnel seek to stop you from asking questions. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't see at this particular page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we can turn to the next page then.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that the questioning of you of Mr. Despodov just go on, you asking questions, Mr. Despodov answering them, and no involvement of Mr. Kuehnel. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I asked some questions, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there was no involvement of Mr. Kuehnel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really tell it from Mr. Kuehnel, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that nothing he could have said is recorded, in any case, on the transcript of that interview?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, this is not an official transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, Mr. Bezruchenko, do you agree that the questioning of Mr. Despodov just goes on. You ask questions, he answers, and there is no involvement of Mr. Kuehnel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that the same pattern here, you asking questions, Mr. Despodov answering them, no involvement of Mr. Kuehnel. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specific questions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, no questions at all. Do you agree there is no one question asked by Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I mentioned before, Mr. Mettraux, I cannot really tell what were the intentions of Mr. Kuehnel at that point of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that, again, this is the same thing: You asking questions, Mr. Despodov is answering them, and there is no recorded trace of Mr. Kuehnel. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we were discussing the various types of weapons at this point of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko, but do you agree what is happening here answer is you asking questions, conducting the interview with Mr. Despodov, and Mr. Despodov answering your questions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asking specific questions relating to specific weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that there is no involvement of Mr. Kuehnel on that particular page. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As would appear from this unofficial record, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, do you agree that it's the same thing on this page, page 32 of the record. You asking questions, Mr. Despodov answers, and there is no involvement of Mr. Kuehnel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It doesn't appear to be any comments made by Mr. Kuehnel, not that I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree with that this is, again, the same pattern? You just go on asking questions of Mr. Despodov, he answers, and at the end of the page, there is a comment that will appear only at the bottom of the page from Mr. Kuehnel? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Who notes that the matter which you were asking questions will be elaborated later. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that you continue to ask your questions without asking for prior consent or otherwise of Mr. Kuehnel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the question was different from the previous one as Mr. Kuehnel suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that you just go on asking your questions from Mr. Despodov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifying questions, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Kuehnel is not waiving or vetoing any of those questions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the end, at line 17, do you agree that at some stage you say: "Okay. Thank you," and at this stage, Mr. Kuehnel starts asking questions again? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And so do you agree that what you did, Mr. Bezruchenko, during this lengthy questioning was, in fact, to conduct the interview of Mr. Despodov in relation to a number of matters which you say are relevant to the case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are probably aware of the fact, Mr. Mettraux, that Mr. Despodov was, in fact, a major in the Macedonian army, and he possessed certain highly specialised knowledge about military matters which were related to the case. The reason of my being involved in this interview was exactly this very reason, and I don't think that anyone except for a military man could actually produce any sensible picture of this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And, effectively, what you were doing by asking those questions, which you believed to be relevant to military matter, is to conduct the interview insofar as it pertained to those particular matters. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Insofar as it pertained to military matter, I was asking some specific questions of military matters. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just for the registry, the document may be taken off of the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that another thing which you did for the Office of the Prosecutor, in addition to your involvement in the interview of witnesses, was to request information and material from the Macedonian authorities on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was involved in various assessments of various documents which might be required, and I was asked my views and my opinions on a number of such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Bezruchenko, but I wasn't asking about any analysis of any document. The question was to the effect of whether you, in fact, requested certain information, material, or documents from the Macedonian authorities on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I did so, well, I don't actually remember if this is the case. But I remember we had a number of discussions with various Macedonian officials and, of course, various documents were discussed, and I might have asked them for some of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that some of those documents, which you, in fact, asked of the Macedonian authorities, had nothing to do with the alleged armed conflict and a lot to do about your case against Mr. Boskoski. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. It could be both.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I will ask you: Do you recall asking for documents which -- from the Macedonian authorities which were not of the military sort but, in fact, directly related to Mr. Boskoski. Do you recall making such a request?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you specifically mention such a document, I probably could give you an answer, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D525, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you see the document on your screen, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you remember seeing that document in the course of the investigation of this case?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have this -- I think I have seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can stay for a second on the top of the document first.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that it's a document that comes from the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia, and that it is dated the 12 -- sorry, I think the 1st of December of 2003. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the title of the document is "To the Office of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, Skopje," and the subject is "Submission of information and documentation in relation to the request from the Office of the Prosecutor." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply to put it in context, I'd like to read the first two paragraphs of that document. It says this: "The Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal in The Hague had submitted a request," and there's a number, "to the government of Republic of Macedonia to provide information and documentation related to cases that were given to the competence of the Tribunal." It goes on to say: "In connection to the received request, the Ministry of Interior within the frame of its competence and in order to completely reply to the submitted request had conducted an inspection of the available documentation with its organisational units; and during this, the following information and documentation are being provided, which we submit to you as an attachment to this letter, one by one, in items as they were mentioned in the request." As you can see, there follows a number of pieces of information which were requested of the Macedonian authorities by the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the second page, please, this would be 1D00-4770, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You can see that the list of answers to your requests just goes on. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not really my request.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, the requests of your office, Mr. Bezruchenko. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the request, to be more precise, of the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Mettraux; not of the office of military analysts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, then, can the registry turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters would kindly like to ask the witness and counsel to slow down and pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, can you locate number 27 on this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will draw your attention the paragraph that immediately follows. It says this: "Related to the request sent by Mr. Viktor Bezruchenko for providing additional annex of the decision number 16.1-3526/1, dated 26 of June of 2001, signed by the Minister of the Interior of that time, Mr. Ljube Boskoski, for establishing the special units of the Ministry of Interior, we inform you that these kind of annexes do not exist, which leads us to a conclusion that these were most probably never completed." Do you agree with that contrary to what you just said a moment ago that the request, at least in some respects, was not the request of the military analyst but that of the Office of the Prosecutor. In fact, that particular request for the annex to a document signed by Minister Boskoski was sent by you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, I have to see this particular document which mentions my request, to make sure that it was really sent by me. But I cannot really agree with you that this document, which we see at the screen now, was drafted by somebody in the office of the military analysis, or, for that matter, in the military analyst team.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, is it your evidence that you did not send this particular request to the Macedonian authorities, and that they could just be wrong about that fact in their own letter?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For this matter, as I mentioned, Mr. Mettraux, I have to see this specific document which you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this was not your only contact which you had with the Macedonian authorities in relation to the investigation of the case against Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had various contacts with Macedonian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you were never just a military analyst, as you seek to portray yourself, but you, in fact, were a contact person and a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor in various contacts which you had with the Macedonian authorities. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: To make a statement like this, you would really have to produce something like a job description for the post of representative to the Macedonian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sorry, perhaps my question was unclear. But do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you received -- to give you a example, you received communications from the Macedonian authorities which were directed to you personally as representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember receiving any communication from the Macedonian authorities addressed to me personally. If you could kindly show such a communication to me, Mr. Mettraux, perhaps I could tell you if this is the case or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 840, please. It has ERN 1D00-7438, and the Macedonian equivalent would be N006-4553.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Mr. Bezruchenko? It comes from the disclosure of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this is a letter from the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Macedonia, more specifically the Cabinet of the Minister of Defence, and that it is dated July the 8th of 2004. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go down the document, you will see addressed to the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, and it's addressed specifically to Mr. Viktor Bezruchenko, Military Intelligence Analyst, Office of the Prosecutor. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So does that help refresh your memory that, in fact, you received communications directly from the Macedonian authorities as representative of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only say that have I received this particular communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, is your evidence that this is the only such communication that you received, or are you saying that you cannot remember whether there was any other?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember if there were any other; but if I received any, that probably was a exception rather than a general rule, because I just -- I have seen this one, for sure, but I just cannot remember if I saw anything else like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, first, let's look at the content of that document. It says this, and it's a response to a specific request: "Attached, and on the basis of the official request from the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY, you will find the requested information for the following individuals," and then there's a list of names. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry can please turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You'll agree that the information which was sought of the Macedonian authority, and more specifically of the Ministry of Defence was a number of phone numbers of a number of members of the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall making that particular request for this information, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. What I remember was that there was a discussion that certain members of the Macedonian army should be interviewed and we should try to draw a list of such persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the effort conducted to locate those people by obtaining their telephone numbers and contact details was led by you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree that you were the one requesting those contacts, those telephone numbers, and the one to whom they were sent by the authorities. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I mentioned, this request was probably drawn on the basis of the information which was in possession of our team, including myself, and related to the members of the Macedonian army which could be interviewed in connection with this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you will agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that a request to obtain telephone numbers or contact details of potential witnesses has nothing to do with military analysis? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you -- it is your evidence, Mr. Bezruchenko, that a request to obtain contact details with a view to interview a particular person would fall within the realm of your role as a military analyst. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm suggesting, Mr. Mettraux, is that there is no evidence to suggest that I drafted this document. There is no signature which I affix to this document, and these are military men in whose interviews I would probably be involved at some stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that the reality, Mr. Bezruchenko, is that from the very early stage of the investigation against Mr. Boskoski, you, and then Mr. Raatikainen, later Mr. Kuehnel, were in charge of this investigation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not be described, I'm afraid, as somebody who was this charge, Mr. Mettraux, for simple reason that I had no executive function.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that your role within the team of the Prosecutor just evolved as the need arose for a new actions or new roles for yourself. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to answer this question, Mr. Mettraux, I really have to know what you imply by my original role and what do you actually mean by saying it evolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me ask you this first: Do you agree that you and Mr. Raatikainen, when Mr. Raatikainen was still the team leader, were presented to the Macedonian authorities as the two contact person competent to deal with this particular case? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand what you mean, Mr. Mettraux, if you could produce perhaps specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let me ask the question first, and perhaps I will try to make it clearer to you: Do you agree that representations were made by your office to the Macedonian authorities to the effect that you and team leader Matti Raatikainen were legitimate contact persons of the Office of the Prosecutor in relation to this investigation? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps, but it really depends on what you mean. I don't remember any verbal statements of this kind, but this is what I can say at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D435, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you recognise this as being a so-called RFA or request for assistance from the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY to the government of the Republic of Macedonia? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please kindly scroll the page a little bit and could you please go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No. We'll stay on this page for the moment Mr. Bezruchenko. Can you please answer the question first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would think that Mr. Bezruchenko should be able to look at the notes before being committed to answer, if he wishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. This would be 1D00-4018, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I can see this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this is a request for assistance from the Office of the Prosecutor to the ICTY to the government of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, as you may have seen from the second page, this would be dated November sometime, I believe the 2nd of November of 2004. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the information which is sought and the assistance which is sought from the Macedonian authority concerns, inter alia, a permission to be granted to interview Mr. Goran Stojkov, is that correct, who is in custody?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply for the record, Mr. Stojkov was at some stage the commander of the Lions unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the request also relate to a report dated 12 of August 2001 signed or prepared by (redacted). Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it also concerns phone records and information which you describe in paragraph 2 to 4 of that document. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps we can turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that that is also what it relates to?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it also relates to a request for transcript of particular phone calls of members of the NLA or Albanian individuals in or around Ljuboten between 7 to 12 of August, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is described as phone record information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that's that one of the requests that is being made in this letter?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would rather read this letter as one complete request to this various items on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that further down, on the second page, the indication is given by the then senior trial attorney in this case that any questions concerning this request may be addressed either to Mr. Raatikainen, the team leader, or to yourself, Mr. Bezruchenko? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So do you agree that, at least as far as this document is concerned, you were being presented to the Macedonian authorities as a competent interlocutor in relation to the matters dealt with in this letter? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would imagine that my name was mentioned in this letter because, among other things, it addresses the issues of the documents in relation to (redacted), a captain in the Macedonian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that what the letter says is that any questions concerning this request may be addressed to you? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this letter suggests that you were represented to the Macedonian authorities as a valid and competent interlocutor on behalf of the OTP, to answer any questions as might be relevant to this particular set of requests. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily, Mr. Mettraux. I don't think that this letter specifically describes my role in those terms which you have just presented, a valid and competent interlocutor. It only says that any questions related to this letter can be addressed to me; that is, I am serving just as a point of contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you agree also, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you have had several meetings with the Macedonian authorities as regard the investigation and preparation of this case?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was involved in some meetings that were held between the Office of the Prosecutor and Macedonian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree, I hope, that several of those meetings had, in fact, nothing to do with the military matters. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you took part in a number of meetings with or on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor that related specifically to investigative aspects of this case which were not military in nature? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We must be more specific about this Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you, recall, for instance, Mr. Bezruchenko, attending a meeting at which the subject of discussion was a security agency called Kometa?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe, but I have to see the appropriate document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D935, please. That is 1D00-7907, and 7905 in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall seeing that document in the course of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll go through this page in any case, if you permit. You agree that this is a document that comes from the Republic of Macedonia, more specifically from the Ministry of Interior, and it's dated the 30th of April of 2004? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is sent, again, to the office of the ICTY in Skopje through Mr. Andrzej Szydlik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters would, again, kindly like to ask the witness and counsel to pause between questions and answers, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Again, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you go that the subject is a submission of information and documentation in relation to the request from the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in the next paragraph, the number of that particular request is mentioned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see only the first page of this document, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. I'm drawing your attention to the first paragraph, where it says that the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY in The Hague had submitted a request number MAR/TO7/MAC-00060-A. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can go further down to a paragraph which starts with the word "In connection to the requested information." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will read that paragraph to you: "In connection to the requested information and documentation included in the items 1 and 7, related to the private 'agency for security of properties and persons Kometa,' as well as providing issued orders by the Minister of the Interior of that time, Ljube Boskoski, these are still not provided." It goes on to say: "The reasons for this were explained to Mr. William Smith and Mr. Viktor Bezruchenko at the meeting on 27 April 2004. The additionally provided information and documentation would be submitted to you." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And does that help refresh your memory about this particular meeting that you and Mr. Smith had with the Macedonian authorities on the 27th of April of 2004?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we had this meeting, but I'm afraid this document is taken a little bit out of the context of the meeting, or at least the paragraph which you are referring to does not cover the meeting in its entirety, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that this particular meeting, in any case, had to do with, inter alia, the Kometa agency and a number of orders said to have been issued by then Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear so, but apparently there were many issues discussed at this particular meeting, and the meeting was not was necessarily limited to this issue only.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that among the other things which you also did on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor is to seize material on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would include, inter alia, some of the material which you've used for the purpose of preparing your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there's another part of your evidence which I would like to go back to, this time in relation to your report. Do you recall that last week, when we discussed a particular aspect of your report, we had a lengthy discussion about what is termed in the introduction of your report, "A military integrated narrative of the events of Ljuboten." Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was at page 6751 to 6754 on the 23rd of October of 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, at that point, I had asked whether you could recall whether or not you had been or that part of your report had been added at a later stage. Do you recall me asking you that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't think you specified at which particular stage it was allegedly added and what you specifically meant by being added.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you recall your answer to the effect that that was not the case and that in fact that particular aspect of your report had been part of the original plan of the report? That's page 6754. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was originally planned that the events in Ljuboten should also be reflected in my report, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that correct, in fact, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this particular aspect of your report was asked of you much later, when the Prosecution thought it important to put before the Chamber a complete version of what it perceived to be the events of Ljuboten of the 10th, 11, and 12th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct, Mr. Mettraux, because I cannot really tell you who was thinking what at various stages of time. What I am telling you though, which I mentioned previously, the plan to cover events in Ljuboten were the original part of the plan for the entire report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that, in particular, Mr. Bezruchenko, you had not been tasked with the responsibility to examine documents and material which pertain to the actions of the NLA in or around the village of Ljuboten on the 10, 11, and 12th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was -- I think I was not specifically tasked to provide the description of the NLA actions, but, in fact, the integrated military chain of events implies that the actions of both parties was supposed to be reflected in this particular section of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that this request on the part of your colleagues to integrate, if you want, that aspect of the evidence was made not in the original plan as you had said, but at a later stage. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think there was any specific request of this nature. I mean the request to cover the NLA, or rather, a request to add the part of the report covering the NLA actions. But as I mentioned, it was my purpose from the very start to provide the balanced picture of what had happened in Ljuboten relying on all sources available, including those of the NLA and the Macedonian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D906, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, what will appear in front of you is the record of your proofing notes with the Office of the Prosecutor on the 30th of September of 2007. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask to you look at paragraph 2 of that particular document, and I will read it out for you. It says this: "Originally, I was not tasked to examine documents and materials pertaining to the actions of the NLA in and around the village of Ljuboten on 10, 11, and 12 August 2001. However, in the interest of completeness, I also reviewed such materials and described them in my report and in the addendum to my report." Do you agree that, in fact, Mr. Bezruchenko, that particular aspect of your report was, as you told your colleague in the proofing session, was not originally part of your task. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have just mentioned, Mr. Mettraux - and I think this particular paragraph fully reflects what I previously said - I was not tasked to examine documents and materials pertaining to the actions of the NLA; but, as I emphasised already, for the sake of balance and completeness, I also reviewed such materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just to be clear, this came later, as a result of a further tasking by your colleagues, Mr. Bezruchenko. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. I was just reviewing these documents as they were coming up.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, just so that the evidence or the record is clear on that point, Mr. Bezruchenko, your evidence is that, whereas you were tasked -- were given a task originally, you did not review or examine documents and material pertaining to the actions of the NLA in and around the village of Ljuboten on 10, to 12 August, but that you decided at a later stage of your own device to do so yourself for the sake of completeness. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This that would be a more or less fair representation of what I said. Well, as you may have mentioned, sir, the role of analyst is to provide an objective picture of what was happening, which is certainly impossible to present without reviewing all possible range of documents available to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think we have touched upon this issue already, Mr. Bezruchenko, but is it correct that all of the information which I used in this particular part of your report, the narrative about what you say took place in or around Ljuboten on the 10 to 12 of August, you received as part of your employment and work with the Office of the Prosecutor? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at all times I was and still have been a member of the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is in that context that you received the material which you used with a view to prepare that particular part of your report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which context do you mean Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I refer specifically to that part of your report called, "A military narrative -- or military integrated narrative of the events of Ljuboten"?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Mettraux. I don't really understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me put it differently then, Mr. Bezruchenko. Do you agree that all of the material that you used for the purpose of preparing that part of your report was obtained through the Office of the Prosecutor and by the Office of the Prosecutor? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the material was obtained the through the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your access to that material was made possible by the fact that you were an employee of that office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it would be impossible otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, looking at from the other way around, there is no material which you received or information which you used in relation to that part of your report which you received outside of your employment with the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really see what you mean, Mr. Mettraux. Perhaps you would like to refer to a specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I should make the question clearer that may help you, Mr. Bezruchenko. There is no one document which you obtain for the purpose of preparing that part of the report that you obtained in a capacity other than as a military analyst. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just so that the record is clear, you agree it is correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, also that you helped the Prosecution team by doing a number of translations of documents for them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily translations as such. Well, I used to make some summaries of certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But do you agree that there is also a number of translations which you did to be provided to your colleagues, to have access to information which they would not otherwise be able to access, by translating orders, for instance?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some drafts which I made, not official; but, mostly, I think there these were summaries, summaries of various books.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, again, that the activities of translator do not fall within the realm of the competencies of a military analyst, as you described them to Mr. Saxon? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps not, Mr. Mettraux, but you cannot really prevent a person from thinking and speaking other languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And another matter which you undertook on behalf of the Prosecutor, and you indicated already, is to review collections of documents. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also selected documents which you considered to be or could be relevant to this particular case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We must have received a lot of documents, of course, and they were all initially reviewed and some of them were selected.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And they were selected by you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them, mostly military documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that all through the pre-trial phase, but also since the beginning of that trial, you have continued to work as a full member of the Prosecution team. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm the member of the military intelligence unit -- sorry, member of the military analysis unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you are also a member of the Prosecution team who -- which is competent to try the case against Mr. Boskoski and Tarculovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you are also being treated as such, for example, as far as training is concerned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which specific training you're implying, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that you received training together with other members of the team of the Office of the Prosecutor? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that all through these proceedings, and in particular since the beginning of this trial, you have continued to provide advice and assistance to this Prosecution team?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was assigned on this case a long time ago, Mr. Mettraux, as I mentioned; and, occasionally, I was asked for my opinion and advice.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Including during the course of the trial. Is that correct, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really tell for certain. I think, yes, there were some instances like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, just so that the record is clear, Mr. Bezruchenko, since the beginning of the trial, in this case, have you been involved if any other case on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this trial began?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was doing various ad hoc tasks as asked by my colleagues in the military analysis team.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you will agree that the bulk of your activities since the beginning of this case have been to assist and to provide assistance as is needed in relation to this case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you did that, in particular, together or with the assistance of Mr. Kuehnel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall I had asked you a particular question last week in relation to assistance which you were asked to provide by colleagues in relation to particular court filings and in relation to particular proposed exhibits. Do you recall our exchange?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that at the time you had asked me to indicate specifically to you the two documents, and the documents were not available, to me in any case, at the time? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that you were saying that you would come back to this issue later.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to come back to it now, Mr. Bezruchenko. Is it correct that, in relation to a particular first exchange of letter between the parties, then a formal application by the Office of the Prosecutor, you were asked to provide advice and support to assist the Prosecution identifying the relevance or otherwise of particular exhibit which were sought to be tendered by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid we, again, have to be specific, Mr. Mettraux. From your general description, it is very difficult for me to understand what exactly you mean. I would kindly ask to you present me a specific document, details, dates, and facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D736, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I'll just go through the letter with you for a moment. It's a letter from the senior trial attorney in this case. It's dated 26th of February of 2007, and it is directed to the lead counsel for Mr. Boskoski, and it is a response to the letter of the Defence of 4th of February of 2007. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may ask, Mr. Mettraux, who is the signatory of this letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can go to the bottom, Mr. Bezruchenko, it is signed by Mr. Daniel Saxon, Senior Trial Attorney. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go back up to the top of the page please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, first, I will ask you this: Had you seen that letter before, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I had seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: To assist you here, if can you read the first sentence of that document, it says that: "The purpose of this letter is to respond to your letter to the Prosecution dated 4 February 2007, in which you asked the Prosecution to clarify the relevance of two separate groups of exhibits." And the letter says that "attached hereto are two spreadsheets."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this is an excerpt from the spreadsheets which were provided to us by the Office of the Prosecutor in response to our request for a indication of relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I could ask the registry to scroll down a little bit to the bottom of the page, thank you, and to focus on what is number 796 it is quite small. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you see the -- Mr. Bezruchenko, the left column 796 refers to the Rule 65 ter exhibit number; the next column refers to the date of the document; the next column concerns a short description and date of the document; the next column is the original ERN; the next column is the alleged relevance of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go a few columns further, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a annotation which is being made "ask Viktor, print ERN, and translate." Do you recall being asked by colleagues specifically to provide information about this document Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please go back to the document's name, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry can go back to the left. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was a question about this document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall whether your colleagues also asked you questions about other documents, Mr. Bezruchenko, that were part of this attempt by the Prosecution to tender documents from the bar table?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we please turn to the next page, and if the registry could please focus on number 802, that would be the third line. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, again, this is the same sort of Excel table. It starts with the 65 ter number, the date of the document, a short description, then the ERN number. It is 03, I apologise, Mr. Bezruchenko, 03 not 02. Then, there is the original ERN, the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can scroll it further to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Again, do you see the same comment, "ask Viktor, print ERN, and translate." Do you recall being asked about this particular document Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please go back to the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be number 803.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall now that you were asked also about a number of other documents, in particular documents that were put forward as supporting material for your expert report? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, there were instances when I was asked to provide my views an opinion of certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that, in the course of this trial, you were also asked for your assistance and support by your colleague in relation to the preparation of a number of witnesses? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically in relation to witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. But if you could give me a example, perhaps I could give you a answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, is it correct, for instance, that you were asked for your assistance or help with a view to prepare a number of, quote/unquote, "military witnesses"? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What do you mean to prepare a number of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were asked to provide assistance to prepare the examination-in-chief of, for instance, of Mr. Mitre Despodov? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would put it slightly differently, Mr. Mettraux. I wasn't really asked to prepare a examination of anyone. I was probably asked to select certain documents which could be used during this examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you did the same, isn't it, for Mr. Djurisic? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I possibly did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for Witness M-051. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you not sure because you can't remember the name of the person?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, Your Honour, for a second?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that you provided assistance of the sort just described by you, in particular in the form of identification of particular document for the examination of Mr. M-051? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, regarding this particular witness, I still am not sure, but that could be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that all through this case from its investigation onwards, you were a multi-tasked member of the Office of the Prosecutor; sometimes an investigator, sometimes a contact person, sometimes a military analyst, sometimes an investigator, sometimes a translator, and now a witness? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only agree to the fact, Mr. Mettraux, that under the legal terms of my job description, my current title is military analyst.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to turn now then to a different subject, Mr. Bezruchenko, one that we have already touched upon briefly at the beginning of the examination, and that, in particular, relates to the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Trajkovski. Do you recall being shown by Mr. Saxon a number of orders and decisions signed by the president -- the then president, Mr. Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm wondering, Mr. Mettraux, whether you are moving on to a lengthy or a short topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm afraid it might be a lengthy, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In that case, it is probably in everybody's interests to have the break now. Can the Chamber observe, Mr. Mettraux, that increasingly your questioning has become somewhat repetitive; and in the Chamber's view, it is becoming unnecessarily so. In simply language, we've got your messages.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I can reassure the Chamber on that comment, Your Honour. I'm moving on to a completely different subject which hopefully will avoid any repetition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. We adjourn now. It would be convenient when we resume if the witness waited outside for a few moments before we coming in, as we want to deal with a matter raised earlier today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We resume late because there was a need apparently for medical consultation during the break. The Chamber would deal with the motion moved this morning by counsel for both Defences who raise a number of issues involving failures by the Prosecution to meet its disclosure obligations. In particular, it is advanced that there have been many new disclosures by the Prosecution in the last three weeks, including disclosure of notes the made by investigators within interviewing various persons over the years since 2001. Some of these are said to have been disclosed in consequence of specific Defence request and some as the consequence of the order Chamber made earlier this month. In some cases, it is said that before the recent disclosure, the Prosecution had earlier advised that no such document or note of interview existed. In some cases, it is said that the disclosure was made too late to enable the material that is now disclosed to be used in cross-examination of a witness or witnesses, to whom the disclosed material was relevant. The delays in disclosure are also said to have presented any or adequate investigation by the Defence and to have impaired the conduct of the cases of the accused. In particular, while the Defences do not seek to have any Prosecution witnesses recalled for further cross-examination, it is submitted that the extent and nature of the failures of disclosure calls for significant action to ensure the fairness of the trial and to adequately reflect the concern of the Chamber at the degree of failure by the Prosecution in this case. Specifically, the Defences seek to reserve the possible need to delay the start of the evidence of a significant Prosecution witness, Mr. Ostreni, and submit that the Chamber should not allow the Prosecution to call an investigator, Mr. Kuehnel, whom it is contented is largely responsible for the failures to disclose. It is further contended that the failures to disclose should be taken into account at the end of the trial in assessing the Prosecution case. The Prosecution in response submits that most matters raised by the Defences were dealt with in its submissions of the 15th of October, relating to the decision of the Chamber regarding disclosure that has been given earlier this months. The Prosecution also had delayed in dealing with the Defence request for disclosure of notes of one interview with a BBC journalist, as it had no record of such a interview or notes; and, therefore, it sought information from a former employee who has now advised that the meeting in question was merely introductory and specific notes or statements were not made, although the Chamber notes that that situation is still being checked by the former employee. The Prosecution contends that most disclosures in recent weeks arose from the matters raised in connection with the motion of the Defences earlier this month, and as a consequence, or, I should say, as a consequence of the specific orders of the Chamber made at that time. In particular, this led to the finding of notes of one former employee of the Prosecution, which have been found on the personal computer drive of that employee and of which there had been no other record. Having been discovered, full disclosure has been made of these notes, and the Prosecution has proposed to the Defences that this former employee should be recalled or, by agreement, his notes admitted in evidence, but neither of these proposal versus been taken up. The Prosecution submits that this should be adequate to deal with these investigator's notes; otherwise, the Prosecution submits there has been no significant prejudice to the Defences, and the Prosecution notes, in particular, that it is not proposed that any witness be recalled. The Prosecution further submits that there is no justification for delaying the evidence of Mr. Ostreni, and that there has been sufficient notice for cross-examination purposes concerning that witness. The Prosecution submits that there is no proper basis for the contention that Mr. Kuehnel should be considered seriously at fault, while it accepts he has erred in some matters. It is not fair, it is said, to seek to cast a large part of the blame on him. In the Chamber's view, the submissions of the Defences seek to make too much of what has occurred and its consequences for the Defences of the two accused, while not detracting from importance of proper ad timely disclosure. Having regard to what has been relied on before the Chamber, in its view, first, there is no adequate justification demonstrated for delaying the commencement of the evidence of Mr. Ostreni. Secondly, the circumstances relied on do not establish any serious fault or wanton neglect or failure by Mr. Kuehnel, such as might justify the significant step of refusing to receive his evidence. Failures of disclosure for which he bears some responsibility may be explored in cross-examination. Thirdly, the Defence should be given -- should give further consideration to the Prosecution proposal to re-call Mr. Tucker or to admit his notes in evidence. Fourthly, and otherwise, if by a failure of timely disclosure, either of the Defences consider that they have been adversely affected in the cross-examination of a witness, the re-call of that witness for further cross-examination should be moved, and any such motion would be considered on its merits relative to each such witness. The Chamber accepts and leaves open the prospect that a failure to make proper and timely disclosure may well be a matter it considers relevant to the weight to be given to particular evidence in due course. In the Chamber's present assessment of the interests of justice, in the present circumstances, the matters which we have identified will be adequate to deal with the disclosure deficiencies that have occurred and to ensure that each of the accused has a fair trial. For those reason, the oral motions of the two accused will not be accepted. We should have the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, due to circumstances beyond everybody's control, it was necessary for a medical examination to be conducted, which has delayed our resumption.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mettraux, you are left with less than ten minutes. Is that practical?

utterances.speaker: MS. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think there is a number of general matters which we could through Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, you will recall I was asking or refreshing your memory in relation to a numbering of questions which were asked you of in relation to a numbering of orders and decisions signed by the president of the time, which was shown to you by Mr. Saxon in your evidence in chief. Do you recall.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember we had the discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that several of those orders or decisions had to do with particular operations? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And several of them were referred to as anti-terrorist operations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think some of them were.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the president, in some of those decisions, Mr. Bezruchenko, referred specifically to the NLA as terrorists or as a terrorist group. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you produce the specific document, I would be able to confirm or deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. I mean, at this stage, there will be no need for that. I will ask you this, then: Do you agree that the president at that time, Mr. Trajkovski, interpreted his constitutional powers as commander in chief quite broadly? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think I'm in a position to agree or to deny that, Mr. Trajkovski [sic], since I simply was not present in Mr. Trajkovski's office at the time. But as would appear to me from analysis of the documents, well, he made certain decisions in pursuit of certain of his constitutional powers, or at least as what was to be believed to be his constitutional powers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me perhaps specify my question, then: Do you agree, for instance, that under Macedonian law as was applicable in the year 2001. The president could only order the partially mobilisation of force, after consulting with parliament? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe under the -- with respect to Macedonian legislation as it stood in the year 2000, the Armed Forces can be used in a war situation which would, in its term, require the parliament to make an appropriate decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful for that, Mr. Bezruchenko, and is it correct that, in fact, Mr. Trajkovski, president at the time, ordered the partial mobilisation of the arm forced without consulting the parliament?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This would appear from the analysis of a number of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, that according to the law as was applicable at the time, the president was required to exercise his command authority over the Armed Forces through and via the Ministry of Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends which law you're talking about, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm referring specifically to the Law on Defence, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're perfectly aware, Mr. Mettraux, that there were two Laws on Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I would like to show you the new law.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, perhaps, for assistance, I will ask the registry to bring up what is Exhibit 1D98, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, do you recognise that Law on Defence as the so-called New Law on Defence, which was adopted on the 1st of June of 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And with the registry's assistance, I'd like to go what is page N002-2797, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bezruchenko, I'd like to draw your attention, in particular, to Article 28 of that law. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in full. I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we will turn the page, Mr. Bezruchenko, when we reached bottom of that page, this would be the next page, but I will read it out to you. The title of that provision is "Command in the Armed Forces," and it's Article 28 of the New Law. It says this: "The President of the Republic is Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces. "The President of the Republic carries out command through the Ministry of Defence in accordance with the Constitution and this Law." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So can you agree that, according to the Law on Defence, the authority of the president to command the Armed Forces was to be exercised through the Minister of Defence? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would also agree that, from a number of documents that you have reviewed in the preparation of your report or in your other capacities, that the president would, in fact, give orders or render decisions to the army directly without going through the Ministry of Defence? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really.
