The document which I have seen appear to have a common tendency, to suggest that, in fact, the president was giving the orders to the Minister only in certainly relations, namely, the moblisation matters; whereas, the orders related to actual operations were given to the Chief of General Staff and sometimes also to the Minister of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Bezruchenko. Is it correct that on a number of occasions, and you've outlined it correctly, when it relates to actual operations, the president would also sometimes go directly to the army, without going through the Ministry of Defence, as he was required? Do you agree with that, that there are a number of orders and decisions which reflect that fact?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say that, in fact, the president would go to the Chief of General Staff, but not as you put it, "the army directly," because the army directly would probably need, Mr. Mettraux, a more detailed qualification.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll ask to you have a look at a particular document which may assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is in tab 24 of the Prosecution binder of documents shown to Mr. Bezruchenko, and I believe it is Exhibit P481.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document, Mr. Bezruchenko, as one of the documents that was shown to you by the Office of the Prosecutor in your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that it is named,"A resolution," dated the 5th of August 2001, and it is signed by the president of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree also that it is dispatched or sent to the army of the Republic of Macedonia for completion of operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation of this document would be somewhat different. Paragraph 1, in fact, states the mission of the army, but it does not necessarily say that the decision is actually sent to the army, as you put it. If you read carefully paragraph 3, it would be perhaps correct to draw a conclusion that the document was actually sent to the General Staff of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is it correct, Mr. Bezruchenko, if you look at the bottom of the page, that this document is dispatched to the Cabinet of the President of the Republic and to the army headquarters, but not to the Ministry of Defence? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should differentiate between army headquarters and General Staff, Mr. Mettraux. These are two different things, and, in fact, I don't what you mean exactly by "the army headquarters." This is one point that I would like to make. The second point I would like to make is that I actually did not see the addresses of this document from the way it is now presented on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, Mr. Bezruchenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry assist briefly by showing the bottom of the page to Mr. Bezruchenko, both in the original and in the Macedonian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Bezruchenko, that this document is dispatched to the Cabinet of the President of the Republic of Macedonia and to the army headquarters, but not to the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, Mr. Mettraux, because in the Macedonian version of this document, the second line under dispatch to, or rather, delivered to should be translated as General Staff, because GS, the abbreviation in military terms, mean General Staff, not army headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, in any case, that this document has not been dispatched to the Ministry of Defence? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. We adjourn, to resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
